authors: Tuomas Ahola, Inkeri Ruuska, Karlos Artto, Jaakko Kujala
definition: Two streams: external to / internal to a project; 'there is clearly a lack of a shared and universally accepted view of what project governance actually is' (p. 1324).
stakeholders: External: project-based firm vs project (agency). Internal: multiple firms with conflicting short/long-term goals + shared mechanisms.
temporality_detail: Governance as 'continuous... process' vs 'relatively static set of mechanisms' (pp. 1323-24); public projects tied to 'political processes that are dynamic and often difficult to predict' (p. 1325).
misalignment_detail: Flags political-process unpredictability and static-vs-dynamic debate; no electoral model.
gaps: Frames the static-vs-dynamic governance question the RQ inherits.
key_quotes: 'there is clearly a lack of a shared and universally accepted view of what project governance actually is' (p. 1324).
Governance as 'continuous... process' vs 'relatively static set of mechanisms' (pp. 1323-24).
coding_notes: The external/internal cut is the field's organizing frame; cited by Bakhshi (2025), Pathak (2023).
